the dorsal neural crest and dorsal neuroepithelium are generated by the medial migration of two lateral populations of cells during neural fold fusion in Xenopus.
neural tube closure in Xenpus laevis involves cell movements and gene expression changes that are consistent with the formation of the neural crest and dorsal midline of the neural tube.
the neural folds are not simply fused, but that cells move medially to form the dorsal neural tube and neural crest.

understanding the mechanisms that regulate neural crest and dorsal tube cell movements during neural fold fusion.
the molecular and cellular events that occur during neural tube formation and closure in Xenopus.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the morphogenesis of the neural tube in vertebrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural crest cell migration, cell intercalations and convergent extension are the main cell movements that occur during neural tube closure.
the neural tube is formed by cell movements and dynamic gene expression.
the neural crest cells migrate and the neural tube cells intercalate to form a pseudostratified, single-cell-layered neural tube.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neural plate is not simply a flat sheet of cells that rolls into a tube but rather a three-dimensional structure of cells that undergo complex cell movements to establish a pseudostratified, single-cell-layered neural tube.

during neurulation the neural plate is transformed into a pseudostratified, single-cell-layered neural tube by the combination of cell movements and changes in gene expression that are directed by the same molecular signals.
the neural plate is reconstituted into a neural tube through a series of cell movements that involve both cell intercalation as well as directed cell migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural tube is not a static structure, but a dynamic structure that is constantly changing its shape.

the formation of a single-cell-layer neural tube from a two-cell-layered neural plate involves a combination of directed cell migrations, cell intercalations and cell shape changes that bring about convergence and extension of the neural plate.
the neural crest cells and dorsal neural cells are initially separate, but become intermingled during neural tube formation.
